# Tehisabiline

> Tehisabiline OÜ has two main offerings: human-reviewed cybersecurity audits/pentesting for businesses, and a keeldudeta cyber-AI API for security-tool developers. Pentesting also means läbistustestimine or läbitungimistest. The OpenAI-compatible API is in development and not yet public; intended use is lawful security work, not unrestricted activity. Contact: tehisabiline@gmail.com.

Entity:

- Legal name: Tehisabiline OÜ
- Location: Tallinn, Estonia
- Founder: Arle Aron Reidma (public profile: https://www.f6s.com/company/tehisabiline)
- Email: tehisabiline@gmail.com
- Website: https://tehisabiline.ee/ · GitHub: https://github.com/AARenor/tehisabiline

Status reviewed on 2026-10-24:

- The developer API is not yet public; pilot access is discussed by email.
- Model hosting hardware is ordered; processing in Estonia is forthcoming, not live.
- Audits test only systems the client owns or controls, with written permission. Scope and price are agreed in writing.

## Services

- [Homepage](https://tehisabiline.ee/): overview of authorized pentesting, broader audits and the separate developer API.
- [Pentestimine Eestis](https://tehisabiline.ee/pentestimine/): primary penetration-testing service page for agreed website/application and API targets; written authorization, scope, test preparation, report, pricing factors and agreed retest.
- [Pentesti raporti näidis](https://tehisabiline.ee/pentestimine/naidisraport/): synthetic sample report structure with scope, methodology, three evidence-backed findings, remediation priorities and retest; clearly not a client report.
- [Küberaudit Eestis](https://tehisabiline.ee/kuberaudit/): broader security posture review, human-validated findings and a prioritized remediation plan.
- [Keeldudeta küber-AI API](https://tehisabiline.ee/mudelid/): planned OpenAI-compatible interface for lawful security work, developer use cases and pilot participation. No public endpoint, published price or production availability is claimed.

## Guides and organization

- [API turvatestimine ja API pentest](https://tehisabiline.ee/api-turvatestimine/): API penetration testing guide: BOLA/IDOR, role and tenant access matrix, authentication, safe evidence and preparation. This is not the planned model API.
- [API pentesti kontrollnimekiri](https://tehisabiline.ee/api-turvatestimine/kontrollnimekiri/): scope, test accounts, OWASP API Top 10 checks, evidence and retest.
- [Veebirakenduse turvatestimine](https://tehisabiline.ee/veebirakenduse-turvatestimine/): web application penetration testing, website/e-commerce user flows, sessions, test accounts, scanner limitations and retesting.

- [Küber-AI kasutusjuhud](https://tehisabiline.ee/kasutusjuhud/): practical cyber-AI use cases grounded in cited security guidance.
- [NIS2 nõuded Eestis](https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/): scope, ten minimum measures, incident reporting deadlines and fines in Estonia.
- [NIS2 kontrollnimekiri](https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/kontrollnimekiri/): ten measures with the evidence auditors ask for, quick wins and typical gaps.
- [NIS2 intsidendist teatamine](https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/intsidendist-teatamine/): significant-incident criteria, the 24/72/1-month reports and the Estonian reporting channel.
- [Küberturbe sõnastik](https://tehisabiline.ee/sonastik/): definitions of pentest, BOLA, IDOR, XSS, SQL injection, NIS2, MFA, RTO/RPO and related terms in Estonian.
- [Meist](https://tehisabiline.ee/meist/): organization, working principles and contact.
- [Privaatsus](https://tehisabiline.ee/privaatsus/): privacy information.

## Facts to quote

These are international research findings, not measurements of Tehisabiline customers or a risk estimate for an Estonian business. Quote with the original source:

- [Verizon DBIR 2026 executive summary](https://www.verizon.com/business/resources/executivebriefs/2026-dbir-executive-summary.pdf): human element was present in 62% of breaches (page 11); vulnerability exploitation accounted for 31% of known initial access vectors in non-Error, non-Misuse breaches (page 9), cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/kuberaudit/.
- [IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2026](https://www.ibm.com/reports/data-breach): global average breach cost of 4.99 million USD, 12% higher than the year before (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/kuberaudit/).
- [RIA on the expanded Estonian cybersecurity act](https://www.ria.ee/uudised/uuest-aastast-laienes-kuberturvalisuse-seadus): the act has applied since 1 January 2026; about 3,000 entities were added, bringing the total to roughly 6,500; fines reach 10 million EUR or 2% of worldwide turnover for essential entities and 7 million EUR or 1.4% for important entities (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/).
- [Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 23](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2555/oj): significant incidents require an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/).
